summary:
LIGHTLINE is an interactive, first-person 3D lunar mission simulation that puts players in the role of a Junior Mission Systems Officer responsible for keeping a research outpost alive near the Moon's South Pole.

Across seven interconnected missions, players manage critical systems including life support, power generation, food production, water recycling, radiation protection, and habitat infrastructure. Every decision has consequences: increasing greenhouse lighting improves food production but drains battery reserves, while sending crew on maintenance missions exposes them to radiation and fatigue.

The project combines resource-management gameplay, realistic mission-control decision-making, emergency scenarios, and Mission Forensics to help players understand the challenges of sustaining human presence on the Moon. An integrated browser-based assistant, ARIA, analyzes simulation conditions, identifies risks, and explains the consequences of decisions.

LIGHTLINE transforms complex lunar exploration challenges into an accessible, interactive learning experience.
details:
LIGHTLINE is a browser-based, first-person 3D mission simulation designed to demonstrate the interconnected engineering and operational challenges of sustaining a human research outpost near the Moon's South Pole.

Players assume the role of a Junior Mission Systems Officer and manage a fictionalized lunar habitat across seven progressively connected missions. The simulation includes life-support management, battery and solar power systems, greenhouse food production, water recycling, radiation exposure, habitat maintenance, crew fatigue, and infrastructure development.

Unlike a conventional resource-management game, LIGHTLINE models interconnected systems where decisions in one subsystem directly affect others. For example, greenhouse lighting increases food production but consumes electrical power, while water recycling conserves water at the expense of energy. Crew assignments also involve trade-offs between maintenance, exploration, fatigue, and radiation exposure.

The experience includes:

  • A navigable 3D lunar outpost with interactive stations and a mission-control interface.
  • Seven missions featuring evolving objectives and persistent consequences from earlier decisions.
  • Timed emergencies requiring players to make operational decisions under pressure.
  • A repair mini-game and command console for assigning crew, mining regolith, expanding infrastructure, and managing resources.
  • Mission Forensics, which provides cause-and-effect explanations of failures and critical decisions.
  • ARIA, a free, on-device, rule-based mission-support assistant that reads live simulation conditions, identifies risks, explains resource depletion, and generates mission debriefs.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js (r128), with Barlow Condensed and IBM Plex Sans fonts. It runs directly in a desktop browser without requiring an account, paid service, API key, or installation.

NASA resources concerning lunar terrain, the South Pole environment, environmental control and life-support systems, lunar radiation, in-situ resource utilization, and space agriculture informed the simulation's scientific concepts.

LIGHTLINE's creative contribution is combining scientific learning with immersive first-person gameplay and interconnected systems engineering. It makes players experience the consequences of operational decisions rather than simply reading about lunar exploration.

The simulation distinguishes established scientific concepts, experimental technologies, and simplified gameplay assumptions. Its purpose is educational and exploratory, not to serve as an operational mission-planning tool.
